articles.title: Meta U-turns on encryption push for Instagram as DMs go plaintext
articles.summary: Linux's 'Dirty Frag' vulnerability broke every rule of responsible disclosure — public root exploit with no CVE and no patches. Peak chaos engineering from whoever decided disclosure embargoes are just suggestions.

articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft's April Patch Tuesday delivered 167 vulnerabilities including a SharePoint zero-day and Windows Defender's 'BlueHammer' flaw. Even Microsoft's security tools need security patches — the irony is *chef's kiss*.

articles.title: We Love Delta. We Hate Delta.
articles.summary: CISA gives federal agencies four whole days to patch Ivanti's actively exploited zero-day. Nothing says 'critical infrastructure security' like a long weekend to fix root access vulnerabilities.

articles.title: Anti-DDoS Firm Heaped Attacks on Brazilian ISPs
articles.summary: ShinyHunters turned Canvas into their personal ransom billboard, paralyzing schools nationwide. Nothing quite says 'welcome back to class' like hackers defacing your login page with extortion demands.

articles.title: Is Canvas still hacked - what is a data breach? The shocking Canvas cyberattack timeline
articles.summary: ShinyHunters hit Canvas *again*, exploiting fresh vulnerabilities to deface hundreds of university portals. Instructure's security strategy appears to be 'fool me twice, shame on... wait, how many times is this now?'

articles.title: Congress Narrowed the GUARD Act, But Serious Problems Remain
articles.summary: Russian military intelligence turned ancient router vulnerabilities into a Microsoft Office token harvesting operation. Classic bear behavior: why break in when you can just walk through doors left wide open since 2019?

articles.title: Big Finance Might Be Dooming the SPLC — Even Before Its Day in Court
articles.summary: Trump's DOJ now treats dodging FOIA requests as a criminal offense worthy of arrest and strip searches. The same administration that classified ketchup recipes suddenly cares deeply about transparency — when it suits them.

articles.title: Hackers ate my homework: Educational SaaS Canvas down after cyberattack
articles.summary: Meta quietly abandoned Instagram's encryption push, reverting DMs to plaintext after years of privacy theater. Zuckerberg's commitment to user privacy lasted about as long as his metaverse obsession.

articles.title: CISA gives feds four days to patch Ivanti flaw exploited as zero-day
articles.summary: Quasar Linux RAT specifically targets developers to poison the software supply chain through credential theft and keylogging. Because why hack end users when you can compromise the people who build everything else?

articles.title: Milestone 1.0.0 Release of APK Downloader `apkeep` Powers Research on Android Apps
articles.summary: EFF releases Guy Kawasaki's Signal guide in English and Spanish, teaching proper operational security to the masses. Finally, someone made privacy tools accessible without requiring a computer science degree and three years of paranoia training.
